note: Statement for T1 item 6, digital partition: every row of signoff/spec/digital-rows.json and the reason its class is not statistical.

rows.reason: The signaling mode is a binary architectural choice. It is exercised by the bit-exact cocotb suites as NRZI encode/decode at the FS rate; a transcript either reproduces the expected bits or it does not.
The period is the arithmetic reciprocal of the signaling rate. It is a derived constant of the design, with no distribution behind it.
Which interface variant the block implements is a declaration about the port list, decided at design time and not measured.
Bus width is the number of declared port bits on DataOut and DataIn. It is counted from the netlist.
The clock frequency is a fixed design input. Whether the datapath closes timing at it is a static timing question answered per PVT corner at the ratified corner set.
Each signal's behaviour is a deterministic protocol rule (handshakes, framing, state reporting) checked bit-exactly by the cocotb suites.
The ratio is a fixed integer. The digital synchronizer's ability to sample at 144 MHz is a timing-closure question answered per PVT corner.
The rail is a nominal library characterization voltage. Digital behaviour across supply variation is bounded by the corner set, with each corner a fixed deterministic condition.
These are logic-level outputs of the UTMI layer. Their value at each cycle is a deterministic function of the transmit state machine and is checked bit-exactly.
The enable is a single logic output sequenced by the reset, attach and suspend state machine; its value at each step is deterministic and checked bit-exactly.
